**Your number n** = the last digit of your student number. If it is 0, use 10.
Write "n = …" at the top of your answers. Tasks 2, 3 and 4 use n,
so every student has different numbers.

## Task 1 · Easy (2 marks)

Which math does the game use? Write **position**, **angle**, **logic** or **probability**.

a) A chest gives a gold coin only 1 time in 10.

b) The ghost is 4 steps above the door.

c) The cannon turns to face the plane.

d) You win the level only if you have 3 stars.

## Task 2 · The grid (2 marks)

Draw a grid: x from 0 to 10, y from 0 to 6. Write the numbers on the axes.

a) Mark the player at P = (n, 2) and the coin at C = (10 − n, 5).
   Write the position of each one next to it. (1 mark)

b) The player moves 3 steps up. Write the new position of the player. (1 mark)

## Task 3 · Vectors (3 marks)

a) Write the vector for this move: **n steps right and 2 steps down**. (1 mark)

b) The player is at (1, 1). It moves with the vector (n, 4).
   Find the new position. Show the sum. (1 mark)

c) The player is at (2, 1). The coin is at (n, 6).
   Find the vector from the player to the coin. Use end − start. (1 mark)

## Task 4 · In a 3D game (2 marks)

The game code says:

```csharp
Vector3 playerPosition = new Vector3(2, 0, 4);
```

Remember: x → right, y ↑ up, z → forward.

a) The player jumps **n** steps up. Write the new position (x, y, z). (1 mark)

b) From (2, 0, 4), the player walks **3 steps back** (z gets smaller).
   Write the new position. (1 mark)

## Task 5 · Think (1 mark)

Your friend says: "(3, 5) and (5, 3) are the same place."
Is your friend right? Explain in **one** short sentence.
